However, the regulation of movement of cargo vehicles between India and Bhutan is governed by an agreement on Trade, Commerce and Transit signed between the two governments on 12.11.2016.
8. Therefore, vital question arises, as to whether the private non-commercial Bhutanese vehicles travelling through India, shall be permitted, with valid insurance documentation in absence of any check post, either of the State or Union, leaving citizens at risk of having Page No.# 5/5 their right to claim compensation defeated.
9.

Act, 1988, the Central Government is empowered to delegate its power to any authority or officer to enforce the aforesaid provisions of law and therefore, the Central Government can exercise such power so as to enforce the aforesaid rules and to ensure Page No.# 4/5 that no foreign vehicle enters into India without any insurance inasmuch as, in the present case, the daughter of the petitioner died in an accident involving an uninsured Bhutanese vehicle.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments: 6. It is submitted that Rule 161 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 mandates that a visitor wishing to have a certificate of foreign insurance endorsed or re-endorsed, is required to produce such certificate before the Customs Collector at a port of entry or land custom post or to such other officer, as the Central Government may, by notification in the official gazette, appoint for the purpose of such endorsement in accordance of the provisions of Rule 1989, and therefore, it is submitted that, the Central Government in absence of any Transport Checking post of the State, can delegate its power to the Custom Department so as to ensure statutory compliance.
